name: Tim LeMaster

bio.statement: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, LeMaster said he retired to Portland from the Marine Corps in 2013.
bio.excerpt: I retired here in Portland from the Marine Corps in 2013.

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists LeMaster's occupation as youth camp counselor and retired Marine, with 22 years in the U.S. Marine Corps from private to major.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Youth Camp Counselor, USMC Ret. Occupational Background: United States Marine Corps, 22 years. Enlisted as Private, retired as a Major.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 52

bio.statement: His pamphlet statement lists a BS in Marketing from Syracuse University and military photojournalism and documentary film production study as his educational background.
bio.excerpt: BS Marketing, Syracuse University Military Photojournalism, S.U. Military Documentary Film Production.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, LeMaster said he would support public safety and police.
positions.excerpt: I will support public safety and the police who help provide that safety.

positions.statement: In the same 2022 survey, LeMaster said Measure 110 either needs to be repealed or fully decriminalizing drugs should be revisited.
positions.excerpt: Measure 110 that essentially decriminalized illicit drugs in Oregon either needs repealed

positions.statement: In the same 2022 survey, LeMaster called for new thinking to help parents get better education choices.
positions.excerpt: we need new thinking to help parents get better education choices.

positions.statement: LeMaster says in his pamphlet statement that voters deserve a government that is effective and frugal with their money.
positions.excerpt: You deserve a government that is effective and frugal with your hard-earned money.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: LeMaster says in his pamphlet statement that Oregon should look to other states' approaches to homelessness, citing Houston's 60% cut in homelessness.
positions.excerpt: Houston’s 60% cut in homelessness in just a couple of years

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: LeMaster says in his pamphlet statement that Oregon should learn from Mississippi's rise in education from worst in the nation to a national leader.
positions.excerpt: Mississippi’s rise in education from worst in the nation to a national leader.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Multnomah County edition), p. 52
